name: Rosewood Kauri Cliffs
insider_take: This clifftop sanctuary sits on 6,000 acres overlooking the pristine waters where the Pacific Ocean meets the Cavalli Islands—golf meets wilderness in spectacular fashion.
whats_special: Home to one of the world's most scenic golf courses, where six holes dramatically play along 200-foot cliffs. The lodge sits on a working farm with native kauri trees (some over 800 years old) and offers helicopter access to remote beaches accessible only by air or boat.
pro_tip: Book the three-hole challenge at sunset—holes 15, 16, and 17 offer the most breathtaking ocean views, and you might spot orcas migrating through these waters between May and September.
dont_miss: The Rainbow Warrior Memorial just 15 minutes away—the Greenpeace flagship was deliberately sunk here to create an artificial reef. Take the lodge's helicopter to Cape Reinga where Maori believe spirits depart for the afterlife, or explore the nearby giant sand dunes at Te Paki.
pros: World-class championship golf course with dramatic clifftop ocean views
Stunning coastal location on Bay of Islands with pristine beaches
Luxurious lodge-style accommodations with panoramic Pacific Ocean vistas
Exceptional spa treatments and outdoor adventure activities
cons: Remote location requires scenic but lengthy drive from major airports
Premium luxury pricing reflects ultra-exclusive positioning
